title: Is the complete-pivoting growth factor exactly 8 for 8x8 matrices?
credit: A. Edelman & J. Urschel 2023, arXiv:2303.04892 (also Cryer 1968, Gould 1991 for the g_n <= n history)
premise_risks: Exact values g_n are cited as known only for n ≤ 6 (g_5 = 4.1325, g_6 = 5); check against Edelman–Urschel 2023 before relying on them.
plain: The worst-case complete-pivoting growth is known exactly only for n ≤ 6 (values 1, 2, 2.25, 4, 4.1325, 5). The value g_8 = 8, attained by Hadamard matrices, is conjectured but unproven, and Hadamard matrices are known not to be optimal at n = 12 and 16. Determine g_7 and decide whether g_8 = 8.
math: With $g_n$ as above (real matrices, complete pivoting), prove or disprove $g_8=8$, and determine $g_7$ (known lower bounds from Edelman–Urschel Table 1).
